elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience (Agreement and/or Order Form)
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund on a pro-rata basis any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term."
Inserted notice is "30 days' prior written notice", shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band (more favourable to Customer)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed anywhere in the redline (condition absent; better than fallback)

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" — no end-of-term Vendor right is granted (stronger than fallback)

reasons: All four atomic preferred elements are present in the single inserted Section 9.4: Customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.

The locked target level (preferred) is fully met; fallback elements are unmet only because the outcome is more favourable to Customer, which is permitted since the two levels are separate bargains and preferred is satisfied.

Minimal: the document contained no convenience-termination clause, so a single concise inserted paragraph numbered 9.4 in the existing Termination article is the least intrusive fix; no untouched sentence was rewritten and no extra exception or boilerplate was added.

Intent preserved: Sections 9.1–9.3 and 9.5 remain effective and the cumulative-remedies sentence in 9.5 is consistent with the new right; no undefined terms are introduced ("committed term" reads naturally against the Order Form term and the Section 2.1 three-year commitment).

Drafting nit (rationale only, not a deviation): Section 2.1's take-or-pay language says the commitment is "without reduction or termination rights", so a "Notwithstanding Section 2.1" lead-in (or a statement of the refund/commitment interaction) would remove any residual argument that the volume commitment survives a convenience termination.
